notes:
I couldn't write these notes: I wasn't able to read any of the source pages.

My first attempt to fetch the pages crashed on a coding error before it returned any content. I had planned to read Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub, Precept Austin, and the New Advent Psalms text. When I tried again, the tool said I had used up my research calls for this turn. So I have no text from any of the allowed sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and give a URL for every point. Writing notes from memory would break that rule, so I haven't drafted anything.

If you ask again (for example, "continue"), I can start over with the research access reset. I'd work through the sources in this order:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** enduringword.com (Psalm 140), then Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** most likely the curses in vv. 9–11 (imprecatory prayer) and the "burning coals" of v. 10. I'd search desiringgod.org, thegospelcoalition.org, ligonier.org, gty.org, the Wesley commentary on wesley.nnu.edu, and lcms.org or 1517.org.
3. **Other views:** the netbible.org notes on Psalm 140, Augustine on this psalm (Psalm 139 in his numbering) on newadvent.org, and catholic.com or oca.org if they cover it. I'd add popular modern teaching only if one of the sites actually discusses it in connection with this psalm.
